report:
## Whole-Body Vibration Therapy and Fracture Prevention in Osteoporosis: A Mixed Picture

Your inclination is understandable, but the evidence is **more nuanced than a clear "yes."** While some studies are encouraging, results are conflicting and major guidelines do not yet endorse WBV as a standard fracture-prevention therapy.

**Supporting evidence:**
- A 2022 systematic review and meta-analysis concluded that WBV "may be a safe and beneficial supplementary treatment for osteoporosis and help prevent fractures," noting reduced fracture risk particularly in healthier individuals ([ScienceDirect, 2022](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0965229922000139)).
- A BMJ Open meta-analysis found WBV reduced fall and fracture risk in adults ≥50, though benefits were strongest in those without chronic illness ([BMJ Open, 2017](https://bmjopen.bmj.com/content/7/12/e018342)).
- A 2024 meta-analysis reported positive effects on bone mineral density (BMD) in postmenopausal women with osteoporosis ([Brazilian Journal of Medical and Biological Research, 2024](https://www.scielo.br/j/bjmbr/a/94WdyWfWNx6yqW8VWdqSgqv/?lang=en&)).

**Counterbalancing evidence:**
- One randomized trial found WBV had "no overall treatment effect on bone mineral density, bone turnover markers, anthropometric parameters and maximal isotonic knee extensor strength in women with postmenopausal osteoporosis" ([Taylor & Francis, 2016](https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/full/10.1080/09638288.2016.1226417)).
- A review noted that WBV's effect on BMD in humans is "not as clear" as in animal models ([PMC, 2015](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4440196/)).
- Neither the UK NOGG guideline nor ACOG clinical guidelines recommend WBV for osteoporosis management ([Springer, 2022](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s11657-022-01061-5)).

**Bottom line:** WBV shows promise as a *supplementary* therapy—particularly for fall reduction—but the evidence is inconsistent, no vibration device is FDA-approved for osteoporosis, and it should not replace pharmacologic treatment. It is best viewed as a potential adjunct, not a proven fracture-prevention solution.
